gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus's advertised 4.4 GHz applies to only one of its five cores (1 P-core at 4.4 GHz; the four E-cores top out at 3.3 GHz), or that this one core gives it a PassMark single-thread rating of 3,197, against 1,879 for the DXP2800's N100, 2,032 for the 8-core i3-N305 and 1,136 for the DS925+'s V1500B. Single-thread speed is the figure that matters for Paper's single-threaded tick.
standout_why: Compared against racksandwatts.com (cited) and esp32.co.uk (cited). Racksandwatts gives only CPU names and RAM ceilings, with no clocks, core split or benchmarks. Esp32.co.uk mixes clock types ('2.2GHz' for the V1500B, 'burst up to 2.9GHz' for the N5095, 'up to 3.6GHz' for the N150). It gives no clock at all for the 8505 and never mentions the P/E split. Neither page has a single-thread figure or mentions Minecraft. ChatGPT's own answer says 'single-core CPU performance' matters but never puts a number on any model. Our current page lists maker 'max clock' figures that can't be compared directly: a 1-P-core turbo, E-core turbos and a no-turbo base clock all sit in the same column.
decides: It confirms the DXP4800 Plus as the pick on a number rather than a clock claim. Its one P-core scores 1.70× the N100 (3,197 / 1,879), 2.81× the DS925+ (3,197 / 1,136) and 1.57× the TerraMaster F4-424 Pro's i3-N305 (3,197 / 2,032). The F4-424 Pro's 8 cores look stronger on a spec sheet, and its multithread score is in fact slightly higher (9,337 vs 8,997), but Paper ticks the world on one thread, so the 8505 wins for Minecraft. The DS925+ costs about the same ($639.99 list vs $619.99) and has the slowest single thread in the table except the DS225+'s J4125. The F2-425 Plus's N150 scores the same as the N100 (1,889 vs 1,879, 0.5% apart), so its '3.6 GHz' buys nothing over the DXP2800's '3.4 GHz'.

findings.label: Intel Pentium Gold 8505 core split and per-core-type max turbo
findings.value: 5 cores / 6 threads = 1 P-core (4.40 GHz max turbo) + 4 E-cores (3.30 GHz max turbo); 15 W base power; 64 GB max memory
findings.source_title: Intel® Pentium® Gold Processor 8505 – Intel ARK specifications
findings.note: The '4.4 GHz' in UGREEN and retailer listings is the turbo of the single P-core only. The other four cores are capped at 3.3 GHz, below the N150's 3.6 GHz.

findings.label: PassMark single-thread rating (Pentium Gold 8505)
findings.note: PassMark lists P-cores as '1 Cores, 2 Threads, 1.2 GHz Base, 4.4 GHz Turbo' and E-cores as '4 Cores, 4 Threads, 0.9 GHz Base, 3.3 GHz Turbo'. The figure is a database average across laptops and mini PCs, not measured in the NAS.

findings.label: PassMark single-thread rating (Intel N100)
findings.note: 4 E-type cores / 4 threads, 0.7 GHz base, 3.4 GHz turbo, 6 W. The 8505 is 3,197 / 1,879 = 1.70× faster in single-thread.

findings.label: Intel N100 maker limits
findings.value: 4 cores / 4 threads, 3.40 GHz max turbo, 6 W TDP, 16 GB max memory (DDR4-3200 / DDR5-4800 / LPDDR5-4800)
findings.source_title: Intel® Processor N100 – Intel ARK specifications
findings.note: The DXP2800's '16 GB max' RAM ceiling is Intel's spec limit for the N100, not a UGREEN choice.

findings.label: PassMark single-thread rating (Intel Core i3-N305)
findings.note: 8 cores / 8 threads, 3.8 GHz turbo, 15 W. Its multithread score is 3.8% above the 8505 (9,337 vs 8,997), but its single-thread score is 36% lower (2,032 vs 3,197); the 8505 is 1.57× faster.

findings.label: PassMark single-thread rating (Intel N150)
findings.note: 3.6 GHz turbo vs the N100's 3.4 GHz, yet single-thread is only 0.5% higher (1,889 vs 1,879). For Minecraft it is effectively equal to the DXP2800.

findings.label: PassMark single-thread rating (Intel Celeron N5095)
findings.note: 2.0 GHz base, 2.9 GHz turbo, 15 W. The 8505 is 2.14× faster (3,197 / 1,492). The TS-464 that ChatGPT showed at $639.00 is slower per thread than the $389.99 DXP2800.

findings.label: PassMark single-thread rating (AMD Ryzen Embedded V1500B)
findings.note: 4C/8T at 2.2 GHz with no boost; 16 W typical TDP. The 8505 is 2.81× faster (3,197 / 1,136). The sample is small (14), so the figure is less certain.

findings.label: PassMark single-thread rating (Intel Celeron J4125)
findings.note: 2.0 GHz base, 2.7 GHz turbo, 10 W. Effectively tied with the DS925+'s V1500B on single-thread.

findings.label: Paper's tick is single-threaded
findings.value: Folia README: 'the current Paper (single threaded) can be viewed as one giant "region" that encompasses all chunks in all worlds'; Folia itself wants 'at least 16 cores (not threads)' and 'a sizeable player count'
findings.note: This is why the single-thread column, not core count or multithread score, decides a friends-sized Paper server. Folia (multithreaded) does not fit a home NAS: it wants 16+ cores and its README says to expect 0 plugin compatibility.
